reviewer.role: bounded independent read-only Discovery semantic WIP reviewer

scope: Read-only inspection of the three frozen WIP modules discovery_plan.py, discovery_candidates.py and discovery_graph.py against R2-R7 discovery semantics, provider target notes and the frozen package. discovery.py and discovery_storage.py wiring were excluded. No source, test, Git, network, connector, Vault or human-gate mutation.

checks.evidence: discovery_plan.py:74-122 regenerates fixed Web and OpenAlex target descriptions, chooses OpenAlex/DOI/arXiv subject precedence, applies the frozen singleton/filter/select/sort/cursor grammar, and enforces the generated OpenAlex URL ASCII bound. query():139-147 preserves declared query order and the 2048-character bound. No arbitrary caller URL is accepted by these helpers.
checks.remaining: Provider held-out capability and exact target vectors remain later acceptance gates; no network execution was performed.

checks.evidence: discovery_plan.py:177-213 calls chosen_id(expanded_ids(...)) before operation-specific capability handling. expanded_ids():21-27 expands an original subject into every identity in a current component. chosen_id():57-65 raises DISCOVERY_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED when the selected namespace contains two values. Therefore a valid completed graph containing an explicit same_work component with two OpenAlex IDs intersecting an original seed makes frontier(), status planning and _choose() raise instead of returning the conflicted candidate as visible graph state/capability gap. The inline probe with W1 plus W2 in one component reproduced expanded_ids -> [W1,W2] and ResearchError DISCOVERY_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED.
checks.contract_impact: R5/R6/R7 require conflicts to remain inspectable and excluded from fusion/preview/expansion; a conflicting component must not turn a valid graph into an unhandled planner exception or fabricate a request.
checks.required_fix: Handle namespace-conflicted expanded subjects before chosen_id and emit deterministic capability/refusal state (or suppress the affected plain operation) while preserving candidate conflicts; do not allow the exception to abort the whole status/frontier.

checks.evidence: discovery_graph.py:178-195 validates only a nondecreasing control.round sequence and round_sequence <= len(self.events). It does not require a control.round to equal the last complete event in its historical install group, and does not verify the R3 event.control_head/preceding-round group rule. discovery_graph.py:197-204 then includes every control with round_sequence < the event sequence, while :206-215 accepts an ancestor control head. Thus an artifact set may contain completed event e2 and a later control with round=e1; the stale group is accepted, and a tampered e2 can bind that control as event.control_head. The same hole exists for a post-event control retaining round=null before the first event.
checks.contract_impact: R3:75-98 requires exact previous sequence, control.round equal to the last completed event at installation, controls referencing an event to belong to the following group, and each event.control_head to be the last control in its preceding-round group. Accepting stale round groups can misclassify user_stop/resume interleavings and permits a stale finish history.
checks.required_fix: Replay controls and events by historical round groups, require each control group to target the immediately preceding completed event (or null before the first), and assert each event.control_head is the last control of its preceding-round group before accepting the complete event.

checks.evidence: discovery_plan.py:271-332 requires an exact predecessor observation, maps terminal outcome to the four frozen retry reasons, preserves immutable base fields, checks cursor against the exact supported predecessor next_cursor, and requires references/related slices to use the original lookup provenance and canonical unseen nonempty prefix. The request key is recomputed from the resulting complete spec at :327-329, so these continuations consume distinct slots and arbitrary changed fields are refused.
checks.remaining: Dynamic predecessor, retry/cursor collapse and arrival-order vectors remain acceptance obligations; no source or test mutation was performed.

checks.evidence: discovery_candidates.py:146-173 normalizes source URLs for grouping, joins known mirror labels transitively, preserves known/unknown classes and sorted fact citations; :176-246 builds one list per provider/seed/lens/operation, chooses one known-first representative per list/candidate, records suppression reasons, and computes reduced Fraction RRF scores with deterministic tie ordering. This matches R6 mirror/list semantics on inspection.
checks.remaining: Parent reports ranking vectors pass; exact all-arrival-permutation acceptance remains a later gate.

checks.evidence: discovery_graph.py:97-113 derives completed projections from the full cumulative graph; :280-285 computes current components and pending introductions before each replay step; :77-86 rejects current-component or completed-plus-pending candidate capacity overflow. discovery_candidates.py:73-104 joins only stable IDs and explicit same_work edges and keeps deterministic component keys. The completed/per-observation no-refund shape is consistent with R5/R7.
checks.remaining: The live workflow/adversarial acceptance vectors, including arrival-order prefixes and 257th disjoint refusal, remain separate gates.

checks.evidence: discovery_graph.py:233-333 enforces contiguous plan/event streams, at most one incomplete tail plan, exact plan/request/observation memberships, cumulative terminal refs, supplied-assessment binding, deterministic child projections, exact event children and final orphan rejection. Pending requests/observations do not become completed events, and current candidate introductions remain pending until event completion.
checks.caveat: The control-group defect DSEM-CONTROL-GROUPING-003 prevents a clean complete-graph acceptance because a malformed stale interleaving can pass replay; the ordinary plan/event complete-vs-prefix checks themselves are coherent.

checks.evidence: discovery_graph.py:118-126 uses the frozen four-reason precedence, inclusive duplicate threshold with total_hits>0, and consecutive completed-stop metrics; :97-117 keeps cited conflicts out of paths_covered. User-stop is correctly kept as a control overlay and complete event rejection at :306-312 prevents a finish from committing under an effective user_stop.
checks.remaining: Control interleaving vectors and exact stop/continue status outcomes remain acceptance gates.

actual_findings: DSEM-FRONTIER-BASE-EXPANSION-002: a current explicit same_work namespace conflict intersecting an original seed causes frontier/status planning to raise DISCOVERY_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED before capability handling.
DSEM-CONTROL-GROUPING-003: stale control.round groups are accepted because replay checks only nondecreasing rounds and does not enforce event.control_head group membership.
limitations_and_remaining_gates: This is a bounded source review; discovery.py and discovery_storage.py wiring were intentionally excluded.
No provider, filesystem, Vault, network or human scientific gate was exercised.
The root-reported focused workflow tests and ranking vectors are not relabelled as remote CI or final acceptance evidence.
The two open findings must be closed and independently reviewed before an implementation acceptance decision.
conclusion: The three inspected modules implement the frozen target, retry/slice, identity graph, mirror-aware RRF, strict admission, replay-prefix and stop formulas substantially, but the seed-conflict frontier exception and stale control-round grouping leave the WIP conditionally unacceptable for exact semantic acceptance.
